title: Find the Range of f
text:
For $f(x) = 2^x$:
- As $x \to -\infty$, $2^x \to 0$ (but never reaches 0)
- As $x \to \infty$, $2^x \to \infty$

Range of $f$: $y > 0$ (all positive real numbers)

title: Apply the Relationship
text:
Domain of $f^{-1}$ = Range of $f$

Since Range of $f$ is $y > 0$, the Domain of $f^{-1}$ is $x > 0$.

title: State the Domain
text:
Domain of $f^{-1}$: $x > 0$ or $x \in (0; \infty)$

This makes sense because:
- You cannot take the logarithm of zero or negative numbers
- The logarithm function is only defined for positive inputs
